en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Maidens (Kumāribhūtavagga) 72.
The Second Training Rule Concerning Maidens (Dutiyakumāribhūtasikkhāpada).
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the full admission to girls who had reached twenty years of age but had not trained for two years in the six rules.
They were foolish and incompetent;
they did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires … [as above] … complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years old but has not trained for two years in the six rules?
… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs are giving the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years old but has not trained for two years in the six rules?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can this be, monks? How indeed can nuns give the full admission to a maiden who has reached twenty years of age but has not trained for two years in the six rules?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence… Having rebuked him… and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:”
“I allow you, monks, to grant the authorization for training in the six rules for a girl who has reached eighteen years of age for two years.
And this, monks, is how it should be granted:

That girl of eighteen years of age, having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged her upper robe over one shoulder, having bowed at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, having sat down on her haunches and extended her joined palms, should speak thus:”
‘Venerable ladies, I, the nun named so-and-so, being eighteen years old and a maiden, request from the Saṅgha permission for training in the six rules for two years.
She should request a second time;
she should request a third time.
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced bhikkhunī:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.

This lady named so-and-so, being eighteen years of age and unmarried, requests from the Saṅgha permission to train in the six rules for two years under the guidance of the noble lady named so-and-so.”
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant the authorization for training in the six rules for two years to the maiden named so-and-so, who is eighteen years of age.
This is the motion.
Let the noble ladies of the Saṅgha listen to me.
This woman, [name], being eighteen years of age and unmarried, requests from the Saṅgha, through the noble lady [name], permission to train in the six rules for two years.
The Saṅgha grants permission to train in the six rules for two years to this woman, [name], who is eighteen years of age and unmarried.
Whichever noble lady approves of granting permission to train in the six rules for two years to this woman, [name], who is eighteen years of age and unmarried, let her be silent.
"Whoever does not approve should speak.
The Saṅgha has granted the authorization for training in the six rules for two years to the girl named so-and-so, who is eighteen years old.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I understand this."
When she has reached eighteen years of age, she should be told: "Speak thus:
'I undertake the undertaking of the abstention from taking life for two years, without transgression...
[and so on] ...I undertake the undertaking of the abstention from eating at improper times for two years, without transgression.'"
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support...
[and so forth] ...and furthermore, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:

“Whichever bhikkhunī should give the full admission to a maiden who has completed twenty years of age, but who has not trained in the six rules for two years, that is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before] ...nun.
...pe... this is the "bhikkhunī" intended in this context.
"Full twenty years of age" means having reached twenty years of age.
One who has become a maiden is called a novice nun (sāmaṇerī).
"Two years" means...
Two years.
"One who has not trained in the training" means either that the training was not given, or the training that was given has been violated.
"Should ordain" means: she should confer full admission (*upasampadā*).
If, thinking "I will ordain her," she seeks out a group, a preceptor (*ācariyā*), an alms bowl, or a robe, or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for the preceptor.
For the community and for the preceptor, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she gives the full admission in a legitimate legal act while perceiving it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If she gives the full admission in a legitimate legal act while being doubtful of it, there is an offense entailing expiation.

If, regarding a formal act that is contrary to the Dhamma, one perceives it as a formal act contrary to the Dhamma and causes [a nun] to leave [the robe], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, regarding a formal act contrary to the Dhamma, one perceives it as a formal act in accordance with the Dhamma, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa).
If, regarding a formal act contrary to the Dhamma, one is uncertain, there is an offense of wrongdoing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if she ordains a girl who is twenty years of age and has trained for two years in the six rules.
"Of one who is insane,
of one who is a first-offender.
The second training rule is finished.
